$comment: char VALUE codegen across all targets (D-CSUBSET-CHAR-STRING-VALUE-CODEGEN + D-CSUBSET-CHAR-INT-WIDENING + D-CSUBSET-BARE-CHAR-SIGNEDNESS-PER-TARGET; D-TARGET-CHAR-SIGNEDNESS-PER-PLATFORM, CLOSED): byte load (movzx/LDURB), byte store (mov r/m8/STURB, baseline pipeline), the char→int promotion, int→char Trunc. `neg=(char)200` then `isneg = neg<0` makes the exit code a per-target signedness WITNESS: bare `char` is SIGNED on x86_64 elf64/pe64 AND on arm64-DARWIN (SExt/movsx/ldrsb → -56<0==1 → 65+66+1=132), and UNSIGNED on arm64-LINUX (ZExt/uxtb/ldrb → 200<0==0 → 65+66+0=131). EVERY row below now asserts REAL behaviour — no row in this example pins a defect any more. WHY THE TWO arm64 ROWS LEGITIMATELY DISAGREE: C 6.2.5p15 leaves bare-`char` signedness IMPLEMENTATION-DEFINED and AAPCS64 leaves it implementation-defined too, so the PLATFORM decides and not the processor — the AArch64/GNU-Linux platform ABI chose UNSIGNED, Apple's arm64 platform ABI chose SIGNED, and clang follows the platform. Signedness is therefore never an architecture property. HOW DSS GETS IT RIGHT (TF-C75): the signedness DSS applies is resolved per (architecture × OBJECT-FORMAT) pair from the target configuration, rather than per architecture — that resolution IS the content of TF-C75. ★ THIS EXAMPLE DELIBERATELY DOES NOT RESTATE THE CONFIG KEYS THAT CARRY IT. The declaration has already been reshaped once and may be reshaped again; these rows must keep asserting the same OBSERVABLE behaviour across any such rework, so what they pin is the resolved ANSWER — UNSIGNED on arm64 × elf, SIGNED on every other shipped leg — and never the spelling of the key that produces it. MEASURED BY THIS AGENT 2026-07-28 on Darwin 25.5.0 / arm64 with Apple clang 21.0.0 (clang-2100.1.1.101) via /usr/bin/clang, every exit code captured DIRECTLY (never after a pipe): (a) `clang -dM -E -x c /dev/null` DEFINES __CHAR_UNSIGNED__ 1 for -target aarch64-linux-gnu, and does NOT define it for arm64-apple-darwin, x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu, x86_64-pc-windows-msvc or x86_64-apple-darwin; (b) `_Static_assert((char)-1 < 0)` compiles clean (rc 0 ⇒ SIGNED) for arm64-apple-darwin, x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu and x86_64-pc-windows-msvc, and FAILS (rc 1 ⇒ UNSIGNED) for aarch64-linux-gnu; (c) this example's exact expression `65 + 66 + ((char)200 < 0)` constant-evaluates to 132 for arm64-apple-darwin, x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu and x86_64-pc-windows-msvc, and to 131 for aarch64-linux-gnu; (d) on THIS main.c clang emits SIGN-extending byte loads for the char locals natively on arm64-darwin (ldrsb ×4, ldrb ×1) and ZERO-extending ones under --target=aarch64-linux-gnu (ldrsb ×0, ldrb ×5); (e) THIS main.c, clang-built and run NATIVELY, exits 132 at -O0 AND 132 at -O2. (An earlier revision of this comment claimed `gcc agrees on both (gcc-arm64=131, gcc-x86_64=132)`; the arm64 half of that conflated arm64-linux with arm64-darwin, and it could NOT be re-measured on this host — /usr/bin/gcc here IS Apple clang — so the corroboration recorded above is clang-only and is deliberately stated per PLATFORM TRIPLE rather than per architecture.) ★ RUNNABILITY ON THIS HOST: only the arm64:macho64 row actually EXECUTES on a darwin host — the runner compiles the other three and then reports that their `runOn` excludes host=darwin. All offset-0 / local-scalar access (no indexed pointer arithmetic), so it runs on every target including arm64 whose lea has only the symbol form. The optimizedPipelines arm proves the value flow survives Mem2Reg (char locals promoted out of their byte stack slots) AND that ConstFold does NOT mis-fold the char compare (the const-eval char-sign twin is tracked by D-CSUBSET-CONST-EVAL-CHAR-SIGNEDNESS).

targets.$comment: ★ THIS 131 IS CORRECT AND ASSERTS REAL BEHAVIOUR — it is NOT a leftover of the defect the macho row below used to pin, and it must NOT be flipped to 132. Bare `char` genuinely IS UNSIGNED on aarch64-linux-gnu, so `(char)200` is 200, `isneg` is 0, and the program returns 65+66+0 = 131. This row is the ONLY unsigned-`char` leg DSS ships, and it is the half of the (architecture × platform) split that makes the split observable at all: arm64:elf64 (131) and arm64:macho64 (132) are the SAME CPU on two platforms, and if those two rows ever read the same number this example has stopped testing the thing it exists to test. It is also why this row keeps an explicit per-row `exitCode` override instead of inheriting the top-level 132. MEASURED BY THIS AGENT 2026-07-28 (Apple clang 21.0.0 / clang-2100.1.1.101 on Darwin 25.5.0 / arm64, /usr/bin/clang): `clang -dM -E -x c /dev/null -target aarch64-linux-gnu` DEFINES __CHAR_UNSIGNED__ 1; `_Static_assert((char)-1 < 0)` FAILS (rc 1 ⇒ unsigned) for that triple; clang emits ZERO-extending byte loads (ldrsb ×0, ldrb ×5) for this file's char locals under --target=aarch64-linux-gnu; and `65 + 66 + ((char)200 < 0)` constant-evaluates to 131 there. DSS reaches the same 131 by CONFIG rather than by accident: arm64 × elf is the one shipped (architecture × object-format) pair the target configuration resolves to UNSIGNED. The RUN itself was NOT executed on this host (this is a linux/aarch64 image and no qemu-aarch64 is installed here — DSS compiled it cleanly, producing an `ELF 64-bit LSB executable, ARM aarch64`); the 131 rests on the four clang facts just listed.

★ THIS 132 IS CORRECT AND ASSERTS REAL BEHAVIOUR. It was 131 until TF-C75, pinned there as the closing witness for D-TARGET-CHAR-SIGNEDNESS-PER-PLATFORM — a silent wrong-value miscompile in which DSS zero-extended a negative bare `char` on macho-arm64 where clang sign-extends. THAT ANCHOR IS NOW CLOSED and this row was flipped 131 → 132 as the proof; the history is kept here only so a future reader knows why this row carries a comment at all. Bare `char` is SIGNED on arm64-apple-darwin, so `(char)200` is -56, `isneg` is 1, and the program returns 65+66+1 = 132 — the same answer as the two x86_64 rows, and deliberately DIFFERENT from the arm64:elf64 row above. The one-unit gap between the two arm64 rows is precisely `isneg`. The explicit per-row `exitCode` is retained (rather than inheriting the identical top-level 132) so that this platform fact stays asserted at the point a reader would edit it, and so it cannot drift silently if the top-level value is ever changed. WHAT MAKES IT 132 IN DSS: the target configuration resolves the arm64 × macho pair to SIGNED, overriding the AArch64 CPU default of unsigned (which is correct only for linux-arm64). Make the configuration resolve this pair to unsigned again — by whatever key currently carries the platform half — and this row silently returns 131 with no diagnostic, precisely the regression it exists to catch. MEASURED BY THIS AGENT 2026-07-28 on Darwin 25.5.0 / arm64, every exit code captured DIRECTLY (never after a pipe): Apple clang 21.0.0 (clang-2100.1.1.101) compiled this exact main.c and ran it natively → exit 132 at -O0 AND exit 132 at -O2 (clang emits ldrsb ×4 / ldrb ×1 for this file there); DSS compiled the same file for arm64:macho64-arm64-darwin-exec and ran it → exit 132 in the baseline arm AND exit 132 under the `full-release-like` optimized arm. Same host, same source, same target, 132 four ways — DSS and clang agree. ★ THE OPTIMIZED ARM IS LOAD-BEARING HERE, NOT DECORATIVE: unlike the sibling char_signedness, this main.c has NO `volatile` seed — `(char)200 < 0` is a compile-time-constant expression — and the optimized arm runs ConstFold. That both arms return 132 is therefore a real result about MIR ConstFold (it does not fold the SExt/ZExt, so the char compare survives to machine code and the codegen answer stands); it is NOT a tautology. If ConstFold ever learns to fold char extensions it must fold them with the RESOLVED signedness, and this arm is what will catch it doing otherwise — the const-eval twin is tracked by D-CSUBSET-CONST-EVAL-CHAR-SIGNEDNESS. Do NOT delete this row, do NOT relax it to accept either value, and do NOT drop the macho leg: a failure here now means a REGRESSION, not a known defect. ★ The sibling example examples/c-subset/char_signedness/ witnesses the SAME (architecture × platform) fact from the other side (its macho row is 10, its elf row 20); examples/c-subset/char_signedness_macro_coherence/ additionally pins the codegen against the `__CHAR_UNSIGNED__` macro so the two DECLARATIONS of this one fact cannot drift apart.
